findings.evidence: TauCeti/Probability/Martingale/Reverse.lean:57-65 (same `public section` context, line 31): `revCEFinite` has body `μ[f|𝔽 (N-n)]` with no `@[expose]`, yet `@[simp] lemma revCEFinite_apply ... := by rfl` compiles and exports. In this very PR `coord` is unexposed but `coord_basis_zero` proves by `simp [coord]`, showing module-local unfolds work without exposure. Convention is stated explicitly at Process/Tail/Basic.lean:157 ('definitions are not `@[expose]`; their characteristic API is the `@[simp]` `_apply` lemmas').
findings.fix: Drop all eight `@[expose]` annotations (keep the characteristic `_apply`/`_mk` lemmas). Consumers already have `Slope.mk`, `mk_eq_mk_iff`, `induction_on`, `congr_mk`, `value_mk`, `slopeOfValue_infty/_coe`, `slopeEquivStd_apply/_symm_apply`, `slopeEquiv_apply/_symm_apply` — no body needs to be unfolded downstream. Use `:= (rfl)` for any `_apply` lemma to avoid downstream defeq reliance. Correct/remove the docstring paragraph at line 87.
findings.issue: `Slope` (137), `Slope.mk` (143), `Slope.congr` (164), `Slope.value` (254), `slopeOfValue` (266), `slopeEquivStd` (320), `FramedBoundaryTorus.value` (407), and `slopeEquiv` (413) all carry `@[expose]`, leaking their bodies — most damagingly the `Quotient (slopeSetoid M)` representation of `Slope` — to importers. The rationale in the file docstring (line 87), that the module system requires exposing every unfolded def for a `rfl`-proven exported theorem, is false.

summary: The characteristic API (intro/elim, _def/_apply lemmas, annotations) is complete and correctly annotated, but eight definitions are needlessly @[expose]d, leaking the Slope quotient representation and helper bodies to consumers.
